source.title: Tucano: Advancing neural text generation for Portuguese
source.authors: Nicholas Kluge Corrêa; Aniket Sen; Sophia Falk; Shiza Fatimah

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present. It identifies itself as a preprint and work in progress.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation perplexity and training loss across model sizes and training checkpoints, and evaluates downstream benchmark scores against token ingestion. It does not fit the scaling laws or compute-optimal allocations described in the original sources.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own loss/perplexity curves and its reported benchmark-versus-token-ingestion correlations. References to scaling results from other studies, and comparisons with other models in Table 9, are not treated as results of a controlled scaling test. The gradient-accumulation experiment in Figure 4 reports changes in convergence, but does not test any listed version’s power-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The study tracks 14 Portuguese benchmarks at checkpoints every ~10.5B tokens for four Tucano models (160m to 2b4) and correlates scores with tokens processed (Table 8). This is a new setting (monolingual Portuguese pretraining) with a direct result on V6. The loss curves (Fig. 5) bear on V1 but have no values and no fitted functional form, so V1 is not effectively tested. The study does not fit scaling laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say larger models and more data improve language modeling. They find that benchmark scores track token ingestion only for CALAME-PT, LAMBADA, HellaSwag and ARC-Challenge, report inverse scaling in some cases, and attribute the weak or negative correlations to invalid Portuguese benchmarks rather than to failures of scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains four Portuguese decoder-only models and tracks their losses and downstream scores at checkpoints, rather than fitting the original sources’ scaling equations or deriving compute-optimal allocations. It reports no power-law exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that gradient accumulation settings and batch sizes changed early loss-convergence rates in small test runs (Figure 4); this is not a test of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation.
record.problems: The loss/perplexity results relevant to V1 are presented as plots without numerical values or fitted laws. The downstream analysis reports correlations against tokens processed, rather than direct correlations with held-out loss; it reports no uncertainty for the correlation coefficients.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 8 correlations were omitted. Table 9’s cross-model benchmark score comparisons and Table 10’s instruct-model evaluation are not controlled tests of scaling with model size or pretraining loss. Figure 4’s gradient-accumulation convergence results were not included as rows because they do not test a listed version’s scaling law or allocation claim.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents and range. Only unquantified loss and perplexity curves are shown (Fig. 5).
Relation of downstream scores to held-out pretraining loss, or to model size across models. Only within-run correlation with tokens processed is reported, with no uncertainty.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope label is dropped: rows r57–r60 are cannot_determine, and the missing power-law fit is an untested part, not a limit. The correlations are computed within single runs, over checkpoints affected by the LR schedule, with no uncertainty reported. Many small or negative values may reflect near-random performance and noise; the authors note ASSIN2 RTE fluctuates drastically from checkpoint to checkpoint. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports loss and validation-perplexity trends across its models and checkpoints, but does not fit a power law, report exponents, isolate parameters, tokens, or compute while holding the other factors fixed, or test several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fitted law is used to predict the loss of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or fitted parameter-count/token-count trends are reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study trains Portuguese text models; it does not test other modalities or compare the power-law form across repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes.
The study correlates downstream benchmark performance with tokens processed at checkpoints, not directly with held-out pretraining loss or a fitted scale variable.
The paper does not test dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup or fitting choices, or whether scaling curves bend away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: CALAME-PT, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, LAMBADA; all four model sizes
relationships.reason: Pearson r with tokens processed is 0.61–0.96 for every model on these benchmarks (r37–r48, r53–r56).
relationships.display_finding: Pearson correlations between performance and tokens processed range from 0.61 to 0.96 for every model on the specified benchmarks.

relationships.condition: ENEM, BLUEX, OAB, ASSIN2 RTE/STS, HateBR, PT Hate Speech, TweetSentBR, TruthfulQA, FAQUAD NLI where correlation is weakly positive or strong only for some sizes
relationships.reason: Correlations are weak (about 0.1–0.58) or strong only for isolated model sizes (e.g., ASSIN2 RTE 0.78 for 630m vs 0.34 for 2b4), so improvement with tokens depends on benchmark and model.
relationships.display_finding: Correlations were about 0.1–0.58 or strong only at isolated sizes, with ASSIN2 RTE correlation 0.78 for 630m versus 0.34 for 2b4.

relationships.condition: Benchmark × model conditions with zero or negative correlation (mostly the 160m model, plus 2b4 on ASSIN2 STS, HateBR and TruthfulQA)
relationships.reason: r is ≤0 (e.g., PT Hate Speech 160m -0.75, ASSIN2 STS 2b4 -0.50, FAQUAD NLI 0.00); the authors explicitly describe inverse scaling (r02, r05, r08, r13, r20–r23, r25, r28–r30, r49, r51, r52).
relationships.display_finding: Correlations were nonpositive, including −0.75 for PT Hate Speech at 160m, −0.50 for ASSIN2 STS at 2b4 and 0.00 for FAQUAD NLI.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The four Tucano model sizes and their reported training runs
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports loss/perplexity curves and states that larger models reduce them more, but the curves do not establish a power-law form or quantify its range (r57–r60).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CALAME-PT, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and LAMBADA across all four models
reader_labels.reason: Each benchmark has a positive correlation above 0.6 with tokens processed for all four models (r37–r48, r53–r56).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Benchmarks with weak, absent, or inconsistent correlations across model sizes
reader_labels.reason: For ENEM, BLUEX, OAB Exams, ASSIN2 RTE/STS, FAQUAD NLI, HateBR, PT Hate Speech, TweetSentBR, and TruthfulQA, correlations are weak or vary across models (r01–r36, r49–r52).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Negative correlations for ENEM, BLUEX, ASSIN2 RTE/STS, FAQUAD NLI, HateBR, PT Hate Speech, and TruthfulQA in the listed model conditions
reader_labels.reason: These model/benchmark conditions have negative correlations between benchmark performance and tokens processed (r02, r05, r13, r20, r21, r25, r28–r30, r49, r51, r52).
